units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
scrambling up on his knees most indignantly.
Look here: Louisa Straker is my sister, see? Wot do you mean by gassin about her like this? Wot she got to do with you?
units.name: STRAKER

units.text: A dramatic coincidence! You are Enry, her favorite brother!
units.name: MENDOZA

units.text: Oo are you callin Enry? What call have you to take a liberty with my name or with hers? For two pins I'd punch your fat ed, so I would.
units.name: STRAKER

units.text: with grandiose calm.
If I let you do it, will you promise to brag of it afterwards to her? She will be reminded of her Mendoza: that is all I desire.
units.name: MENDOZA

units.text: This is genuine devotion, Henry. You should respect it.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: fiercely.
Funk, more likely.
units.name: STRAKER

units.text: springing to his feet.
Funk! Young man: I come of a famous family of fighters; and as your sister well knows, you would have as much chance against me as a perambulator against your motor car.
units.name: MENDOZA

units.text: secretly daunted, but rising from his knees with an air of reckless pugnacity.
I ain't afraid of you. With your Louisa! Louisa! Miss Straker is good enough for you, I should think.
units.name: STRAKER

units.text: I wish you could persuade her to think so.
units.name: MENDOZA

units.text: exasperated.
Here--
units.name: STRAKER

units.text: rising quickly and interposing.

Oh come, Henry: even if you could fight the President you can't fight the whole League of the Sierra. Sit down again and be friendly. A cat may look at a king; and even a President of brigands may look at your sister. All this family pride is really very old fashioned.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: subdued, but grumbling.
Let him look at her. But wot does he mean by makin out that she ever looked at im?
units.name: STRAKER

units.text: Reluctantly resuming his couch on the turf.
Ear him talk, one ud think she was keepin company with him.
units.name: STRAKER

units.text: He turns his back on them and composes himself to sleep.
to Tanner, becoming more confidential as he finds himself virtually alone with a sympathetic listener in the still starlight of the mountains; for all the rest are asleep by this time.

It was just so with her, sir. Her intellect reached forward into the twentieth century: her social prejudices and family affections reached back into the dark ages. Ah, sir, how the words of Shakespear seem to fit every crisis in our emotions!
units.name: MENDOZA

units.text: I loved Louisa: 40,000 brothers Could not with all their quantity of love Make up my sum.
And so on.
I forget the rest.
Call it madness if you will--infatuation.
I am an able man, a strong man: in ten years I should have owned a first-class hotel.
I met her; and you see!
I am a brigand, an outcast.
Even Shakespear cannot do justice to what I feel for Louisa.
Let me read you some lines that I have written about her myself.

However slight their literary merit may be, they express what I feel better than any casual words can. [He produces a packet of hotel bills scrawled with manuscript, and kneels at the fire to decipher them, poking it with a stick to make it glow].
clapping him rudely on the shoulder.
Put them in the fire, President.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: startled.
Eh?
units.name: MENDOZA

units.text: You are sacrificing your career to a monomania.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I know it.
units.name: MENDOZA

units.text: No you don't. No man would commit such a crime against himself if he really knew what he was doing. How can you look round at these august hills, look up at this divine sky, taste this finely tempered air, and then talk like a literary hack on a second floor in Bloomsbury?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: shaking his head.
The Sierra is no better than Bloomsbury when once the novelty has worn off. Besides, these mountains make you dream of women--of women with magnificent hair.
units.name: MENDOZA

units.text: Of Louisa, in short. They will not make me dream of women, my friend: I am heartwhole.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Do not boast until morning, sir. This is a strange country for dreams.
units.name: MENDOZA

units.text: Well, we shall see. Goodnight.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: He lies down and composes himself to sleep.
Mendoza, with a sigh, follows his example; and for a few moments there is peace in the Sierra.
Then Mendoza sits up suddenly and says pleadingly to Tanner--
Just allow me to read a few lines before you go to sleep. I should really like your opinion of them.
units.name: MENDOZA

units.text: drowsily.
Go on. I am listening.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I saw thee first in Whitsun week Louisa, Louisa--
units.name: MENDOZA
